sources.title: Wałęsa address and answers to PACE
sources.evidence: Defended democracy, market transition with recession relief, reciprocal European trade, minority language education and Catholic public identity while acknowledging Church-state separation.

sources.title: 1983 Nobel Peace Prize: Lech Wałęsa
sources.evidence: Awarded for nonviolent struggle for independent unions and human rights; arrested after Solidarity was banned.

sources.title: Jerzy Regulski, Local Government Reform in Poland: An Insider’s Story
sources.evidence: Participant history describes the 1995 presidential campaign and Wałęsa presidential constitutional draft proposing three tiers of local government, the most far-reaching local-government draft; not a proposal for sovereign federal states.

sources.title: Amnesty International Report 1996: Poland
sources.evidence: Reporting 1995: Wałęsa opposed reduction of presidential powers. Death-penalty moratorium entered force in November, but report does not establish his personal position on capital punishment.

sources.title: Wałęsa blocks abortion liberalisation
sources.evidence: Vetoed amendment on July 4 allowing abortion for serious material or personal hardship.

sources.title: Wałęsa vows to fight antisemitism, acknowledging his contribution
sources.evidence: Acknowledged campaign wording identifying himself as wholly Polish had encouraged antisemitic impressions; pledged reconciliation with Jews and grounded it in religion.

sources.title: Joint remarks in Warsaw
sources.evidence: Wałęsa invited General Motors and General Electric investment and welcomed US security assurances; joint discussion covered NATO Partnership for Peace, market transition and relief for unemployed workers.

sources.title: Poland country report to Earth Summit
sources.evidence: Records Wałęsa’s presidential patronage of the 1994 environmental community contest, organised with provincial offices to encourage local sustainable-development action.

sources.title: Commanding Heights interview with Lech Walesa
sources.evidence: Retrospective account of market transition: communist investment ignored economic viability, modern equipment could be badly located and systemic change hurt workers. Used only as retrospective testimony about the defined period.

sources.title: Le Monde interview on reforms and union independence
sources.evidence: Supported democratic safeguards and market reform but insisted Solidarity should defend workers independently of government; wanted an active president accelerating reform.

sources.title: RFE/RL Newsline: Constitutional Tribunal and broadcasting
sources.evidence: Reports tribunal ruling that Wałęsa had unlawfully removed the National Broadcasting Council chairman, complicating a purely civil-libertarian portrayal.

sources.title: Un chemin d’espoir: publisher catalogue
sources.evidence: Publisher identifies Lech Walesa as author and April 22 1987 publication.

sources.title: Um caminho de esperança: Brazilian library catalogue
sources.evidence: TJRJ library identifies Lech Walesa, translator Jusmar Gomes, Best Seller São Paulo 1987, Brazilian title and French original.

sources.title: A Way of Hope bibliography
sources.evidence: Henry Holt 1987 English edition; autobiography covering Solidarity and Polish political struggle, not solely personal life.

sources.title: Wałęsa protests treatment of Zelenskyy
sources.evidence: Current-context check confirms later political activity; excluded from this 1980–1995 historical model. Later LGBT and refugee comments were likewise excluded.

facts: Presidential constitutional proposal envisaged three levels of territorial self-government.
estrutura.tension: Local autonomy did not mean secession, sovereign state constitutions or abandoning national law.

facts: Led the movement for free elections but fought reductions in presidential authority.
representacao.tension: Democratic mandate and opposition rights coexist with impatience toward parliamentary and institutional restraint.

facts: Persecuted union organiser; later presidential interference with broadcasting was ruled unlawful.
poder.tension: Opposition to political repression did not imply libertarian permissiveness on drugs, euthanasia or policing.

facts: Defended minority language education and repudiated antisemitism after divisive campaign language.
imigracao.tension: Pluralism alongside strong Polish Catholic identity; no basis for importing 2015 refugee opinions.

facts: Nonviolent resistance and support for Western collective security.
diplomacia.tension: Negotiation first while retaining armed defense; neither unilateral disarmament nor aggressive warfare.

facts: Sought American security commitments and NATO integration.
intervencao.tension: Rejects Soviet domination and aggressive nationalism, but not alliances or diplomatic pressure.

facts: Supported privatisation and foreign investors while maintaining independent worker representation.
economia.tension: Private enterprise does not entail privatising police or eliminating the safety net.

facts: Supported market transition but called for more active state financial resources against recession.
controle.tension: Neither central planning nor absolute laissez-faire; labour bargaining and public stabilisation remain legitimate.

facts: Pressed Western Europe to open markets reciprocally and invited US industrial investment.
comercio.tension: Open trade with concerns about one-sided import competition and social costs, not autarky.

facts: Invoked Catholic identity publicly but also affirmed Church-state separation.
religiao.tension: Strong personal and public religious values without a straightforward endorsement of theocracy.

moral.tension: Catholic family morality should not be confused with all later views on sexuality; exact positions on modern identity policies remain inferred.

facts: Sought modern industrial investment; sponsored local environmental projects in 1994.
tecnologia.tension: Industrial modernisation combined with environmental stewardship and Catholic bioethical limits, not unbounded transhumanism.

limitations: Historical model: later public positions excluded even though current activity checked through 2026-10-01.
Modern Brazil-specific items, AI, crypto and gene enhancement require analogical judgments, not claimed direct historical statements.
No verified personal death-penalty statement in the period; state moratorium is not attributed as personal advocacy.
Technology and detailed migration rules are weaker than economic and constitutional evidence; dedicated searches performed.
Regulski is a participant account published later; PBS is retrospective testimony, used only for events in the historical period.

recommendedMetadata.reason: PT and EN accurately describe the explicit historical scope; coordinator notified before answering.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political autobiography about Solidarity and resistance to communist rule; 1987 first edition verified against publisher and Brazilian library. No existing books.json entry found.

title.pt: Um caminho de esperança: uma autobiografia

processNotes: Single independent audit; no stored answer archives, vectors, similarity reviews or numerical reports consulted. Existing research read only for profilePeriod and source URLs.
Research and metadata check completed before answers.

Likely conceptual neighbours: Havel (shared dissident democracy, less Catholic and presidential); Adenauer (Christian Atlanticism but different union and territorial context); Thatcher (market reform but stronger union and welfare commitments here). These are factual distinctions, never numerical targets.

All 240 answers and five archetypes written after research. Original validator passes with three nonblocking similarity warnings. No answer changes after seeing validation; Catholic Atlanticist overlap accepted. Local-government reform, independent union origins and presidential conflicts supply substantive distinctions. No shared files or archives modified.
